summary: Dedicated capacity throughput degradation causing latency regressions and request timeouts for Acme Labs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acme Labs reports sudden degradation in throughput on their Dedicated capacity pool resulting in increased tail latency and intermittent request timeouts (streaming disconnects and 5xx).

Impact:
- Multiple customer production routes experiencing 2x-5x higher p95/p99 token latency since ~2026-03-02 03:00 UTC.
- Several requests returned 504/5xx during heavy traffic windows; customer reports user-visible errors.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: dedicated-us-east-acme-01
- Region: us-east-1
- Model variants: redwood/gpt-neo-2.7b (quantized) and redwood/gpt-j-6b

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send steady ramped traffic to Acme's endpoint (configured at 40 RPS sustained).
2) Observe increased queueing and rising token latencies after ~10-15 minutes.
3) Occasional streaming disconnects and 504s reported by client SDK.

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler did not add additional GPUs despite queue depth exceeding configured thresholds.
- GPU utilization on some hosts reached >95% while others showed low utilization (~10-20%), indicating imbalanced placement.
- NVSM metrics show long kernel execution times on a subset of pods.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should add nodes or rebalance workload before request timeouts.
- Load should be distributed to avoid single-host contention.

Logs/metrics (summary):
- Serving-runtime traces show increased lock wait times and contended memory bandwidth on hosts i-0a1b2c3d (high) vs i-0d4e5f6g (low).
- Scheduler logs: several placement failures and pod restarts between 02:50-03:20 UTC.
- Autoscaler events: threshold breached at 02:58 UTC but scale-up action delayed until 03:30 UTC (failed due to resource quota).

Initial hypothesis:
- Noisy neighbor causing GPU contention on a subset of machines combined with a mis-sized autoscaling configuration and a quota/placement bug that prevented timely scale-up.
- Potential kernel-level regression in runtime (PR referenced) increasing execution time for certain model ops under contention.

investigation_notes: Collected full serving-runtime traces and NVSM profiles from affected hosts for 02:30-04:00 UTC window.

Pinned high GPU kernel latencies to a small set of pods running redwood/gpt-j-6b with long context lengths; kernels show longer memcpy and attention kernel times when co-located with another high-memory job.
Autoscaler logs show 'InsufficientQuota' errors from cloud provider between 02:58-03:20 UTC; request for new instances timed out and then retried. Quota request was pending for the account.
Scheduler placement algorithm allowed multiple high-memory pods per host due to incorrect bin-packing of memory pressure metric (regression introduced in scheduler v2.4.1).

Related runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2143 identified small change to attention kernel dispatch that increases memory copies under heavy page fault conditions; needs verification.
Reproduced noisy-neighbor effect in staging by co-locating a synthetic heavy-memory job; observed similar p99 latency increases and kernel time growth.

[autoscaler] 2026-03-02T03:00:05Z INFO threshold breach queue_depth=420 target_replicas=8 requested_replicas=8 status=delayed
resolution:
Mitigations applied (temporary):
- Manually drained noisy workloads from affected GPU hosts and pinned Acme's pods to healthy hosts.
- Requested and received emergency quota increase for us-east-1 to allow autoscaler to add nodes.
- Deployed scheduler patch (rollout v2.4.2) to improve bin-packing of memory_pressure metric and avoid co-locating high-memory pods.

Permanent work and next steps:
- Runtime team to revert/patch PR #2143 and run focused kernel-level benchmarks under co-location (owner: Emma Li, expected ETA 2026-03-07).
- Autoscaler telemetry to add faster failure path and alert on InsufficientQuota (owner: SRE team, ETA 2026-03-05).
- Add placement guardrail to prevent >1 high-memory-inference pod per GPU host for dedicated pools (owner: scheduler team, ETA 2026-03-06).
- Follow-up with Acme Labs to schedule a controlled load test and confirm stability; plan for rolling restart of affected pool during low-traffic window.
- Post-incident: produce postmortem and update runbook (link will be attached) and notify customers affected by the event.
Customer status: Acme Labs confirmed error rate reduced and accepted temporary workaround; awaiting confirmation after controlled test.
